paper.title: A general theory of bibliometric and other cumulative advantage processes
paper.journal: Journal of the American Society for Information Science 27(5):292-306

headline: Price 1976 cumulative-advantage citation model (agent-based): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; never-cited p0=0.571 (analytic 0.571), tail gamma-hat=2.21 vs m=1 contrast 2.73; constant out-degree m=3, k_max~2734

verdicts.gate: P1 directed DAG + constant out-degree: non-seed out-degree exactly m (var~0), k_max in [40,400], Var(in)/Var(out)>50
reasons: non-seed out-degree all == m: True; out-degree var ~ 0: True; k_max per seed = [2841, 3381, 1979] (band [40,400]); Var(in)/Var(out) per seed = [261997.4, 274241.9, 233020.4] (need > 50.0)

verdicts.gate: P2 large never-cited mass: zero-in-degree fraction in [0.52,0.62] (analytic 4/7~0.571; BA gives 0)
P3 tunable heavy tail gamma<3: KS-selected discrete-MLE gamma-hat in [2.1,2.9] at m=3, and higher at the m=1 contrast (a/m tunability)

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the FIRST cumulative-advantage network (directed DAG, large never-cited mass, tunable gamma<3) and would catch an artifact, and how it is distinct from BA

citations: Price, D. J. de Solla (1976). A general theory of bibliometric and other cumulative advantage processes. Journal of the American Society for Information Science 27(5):292-306. doi:10.1002/asi.4630270505.
Price, D. J. de Solla (1965). Networks of scientific papers. Science 149(3683):510-515.
Newman, M. E. J. (2010). Networks: An Introduction (Oxford Univ. Press), ch. 14 (Price model master-equation derivation of gamma = 2 + a/m).
Clauset, A., Shalizi, C. R. & Newman, M. E. J. (2009). Power-law distributions in empirical data. SIAM Review 51(4):661-703.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against finite-size-robust structural signatures (constant out-degree, never-cited mass, in/out variance ratio) plus the CSN KS-selected tail exponent
